analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 1031-1535). They contain only historical release notes and are documentation, with no executable source change. I read both units against the threat model and found no security regression.

The notes mention security-relevant behaviors that the code diff must be reviewed for elsewhere:
- A dev/staging installer signature relaxation (scripts/install.sh, lines ~1263) for `-dev.` and `-staging.` versions. It keeps the bundle identifier pinned and keeps production on the full Apple-team requirement. This touches T-013, T-034 and TB-013/T-061 (installer tampering). The relaxation is not in the supplied text, so whether it can be triggered by a crafted version string on a production path is unverified.
- A staging lane and a dev-branch lane in CI that sign with the shared Developer-ID certificate. The notes say prod stays tag-gated and that the dev-branch lane carries no production secret. These claims are unverified here (A-011, A-017 related).
- The cold-load queue release (line ~1150), which lets resident-model requests, cancels and attestation challenges proceed during a load. This relates to the TB-011 availability and T-053 cancel/challenge ordering.
- The SSD checkpoint staging cap raised to 7 GiB / 15 s on Macs with 48 GiB or more (line ~1207), and the namespace change for GPT-OSS checkpoints. These relate to T-041 (at-rest artifacts and the staging memory bound). The notes keep the daily write cap, HMAC naming and TTL unchanged.
- Segment retention and the proactive buffer-cache sweep (lines ~1165-1166), which may affect T-028 (residual GPU memory). Retained segments are reported as uncommitted and zero-filled on demand, which is a possible residual-data question for the code review.
- The streamed tool calls, template-loop and prompt-token caching changes are noted as being validated against the previous path.

No canonical-definition changes are visible in these units. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the code diff behind these claims needs a separate pass; needs_deeper_review is set only for that reason.
